# TempoStep

> An iPhone metronome that listens. When you stop playing, the tempo steps up on its own.

TempoStep raises the tempo step by step as you practice. It uses the iPhone microphone to hear when you stop. After a short silence the tempo moves; when you start again, the next tempo is already running.

Made by Alan Molina, an orchestral violinist who got tired of stopping mid-passage to reset the metronome by hand.

- Platform: iPhone, iOS 17 or later
- Price: $4.99, paid once. No subscription, no ads.
- Version: 1.0
- Support: tempostepapp@gmail.com

## How a session runs

1. Play. Set a starting tempo and press start. It measures the room for two seconds, then the click runs and the mic listens.
2. Pause. Stop playing. TempoStep hears the quiet and counts down.
3. Step. The tempo moves by the step you set. The screen flashes to another color for about a second. Start playing and the new tempo is already running.
4. Target. At your target you get a chime, three haptic taps and the sentence "target reached."

## Practice modes

- Step Up (default): adds your step each time you stop, up to a target.
- Shuffle: picks a random tempo within 10, 20 or 30 percent of the target on every stop. Based on research on interleaved practice (Carter & Grahn, 2016; Mathias & Goldman, 2025).
- Spiral: climbs three steps, drops back by 25 percent, 50 percent or all the way, then climbs on.
- Step Down: works down from a fast tempo to a floor you set.

All four use the same microphone trigger.

## Other features

- Microphone calibration: a two-second room measurement each time you press start.
- Background audio: auto advance keeps working while you use forScore, IMSLP, a tuner or another app.
- Manual mode: listening off, no calibration. Press next to move up and back to return.
- Tap tempo: tap along a few times to match a reference.
- Hold tempo: the lock keeps the tempo in place while it keeps listening. Auto mode only.
- Subdivisions: none, 8ths, triplets or 16ths.
- Metres: 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 5/4, 6/8, 7/8, 9/8 and 12/8 from a picker under the tempo. Compound metres accent every third beat.
- Seven color themes: yellow (default), green, coral, sky, lilac, paper, ink.
- Two click sounds: woodblock and tactus.
- Controls hide after three seconds of playing. Tap the screen to bring them back. Long-press any control for a help card.

## How it differs from ramp apps

Some metronome apps raise the tempo on a bar count or a timer. TempoStep raises it when you stop, so the break between passes is yours.
